title: Chronos: timebound fallback orchestrator and region-aware SLO recovery (hotfix)
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduces Chronos fallback orchestrator (timebound failover windows) and fixes a race in regional egress handoff. Improves telemetry for SLO-driven recovery. Backported as a hotfix to main.
description:
Motivation: Recent incidents showed oscillation during cross-region failovers when short-lived spikes triggered full circuit handoffs. Chronos is a small orchestrator that enforces timebound fallback windows and a coordinated recovery policy per-region to avoid repeated rapid circuit flips and egress thrashing.

This PR delivers: 1) a timebound fallback orchestrator (Chronos) that gates full failover for a configurable 'snooze' window; 2) a coordinated recovery probe sequence to reintroduce capacity gradually; 3) tighter egress cap smoothing during handoff to avoid transient egress storms; 4) tracing and metric hooks to make recovery windows and decisions visible in the Console; 5) a race-condition hotfix when two adjacent regions try to claim the same tenant lease during rapid handover.

Checklist:
- [x] core orchestrator loop implemented
- [x] policy config + Linear-driven defaults added
- [x] telemetry metrics & tracing added
- [x] unit tests for lease arbitration and window expiry
- [x] integration smoke against regional failover simulator
- [x] rollout gating and feature flagging
- [x] documentation notes for operators (Console + CLI)

Implementation notes: Chronos runs inside the control-plane failover coordinator and exposes a small policy struct (TimeboundWindow) used during SLO-triggered decisions. The orchestrator prefers soft-fallback first (prefix shedding / KV-preserve) and only escalates to full region handoff if the snooze window expires without observed improvement. During rejoin, Chronos uses a backoff ladder that increases allowed egress gradually over a window instead of an immediate cold restore. This avoids KV cache thrash and sudden downstream egress spikes.

Commit summary:
- 9f2b7c9: introduce chronos orchestrator scaffolding and policy config
- d2a3b4e: implement lease arbitration + timebound window state machine
- 7c5e1d2: add egress smoothing and staged reintroduce logic
- a1b9f0f: telemetry: metrics + tracing spans + Console dashboard wiring
- c3d4e5f: tests: unit + integration for snooze semantics
- f0e1d2a: hotfix: atomic lease claim to prevent double-claim race (edge case found during CI)

Changed areas (high level):
- runtime/eviction/chronos_orchestrator.go: core state machine and gating logic
- controlplane/failover/lease_arbitrator.go: atomic claim API and backpressure signals
- controlplane/failover/timebound_policy.go: policy structs and defaults
- observability/metrics/chronos_metrics.yaml: metrics definitions for recovery windows and counters
- tracing/spans/chronos_span_helpers.go: small helpers for span attributes
- infra/simulator/regional_failover_sim.go: new simulator harness for integration tests
- cmd/console/dashboards/chronos_recovery.md: operator facing notes and screenshot instructions
- docs/ops/chronos.md: operator guide and rollout steps
- tests/integration/chronos_snooze_test.go: integration scenarios

Summary of behavioral changes:
- Default snooze window: 12s (configurable per-tenant/class)
- Staged reintroduce steps: 25% -> 50% -> 100% egress allowance over configurable intervals
- Preference order: soft-degrade -> staged reintroduce -> full region failover (last resort)

Backwards compatibility: guarded by feature flag "chronos.failover_window" defaulting to enabled for canary rings and off for GA until operator opt-in. Rollout plan in docs/ops/chronos.md.

CI: initial runs failed on a flaky simulator test (race in test harness). I fixed the harness and re-ran CI; final green. See CI checkpoints below.

Review conversation (selection): "Ayesha Patel": "High level: this seems like the right move to reduce oscillation. A few questions: can we make snooze window tenant-configurable and ensure we don't block small tenants?" "Maya Thompson": "Answer: yes; policy supports per-tenant overrides with safe bounds (min/max) and defaults tuned for our medium/large tenants. Added docs to cover operator knobs." "Diego Ramos": "Telemetry looks fine; can we emit an event when Chronos promotes staged reintroduce so Debugging SLO regressions becomes easier?" "Maya Thompson": "Added chronos.reintroduce_promote event counter; wired to Console alerts in metrics yaml." "Sara Liu": "Found a race when two regions tried to claim lease in v1; tests caught it but please ensure hotfix is backported to main which we need for the incident roll-forward." "Maya Thompson": "Backported atomic claim fix and added integration tests that failed before but pass now."

CI checks and timeline:
- unit-tests: pass
- integration/sim: initially failed (race in simulator harness)
- integration/sim: fixed and re-run: pass
- lint: pass
- e2e-regional: pass (canary ring)

Post-merge notes: merged to main via squash on 2026-02-22. Operator docs updated and an emergency rollback plan is included (disable feature flag + graceful drain).

Observability: new metrics (chronos_snooze_active_total, chronos_reintroduce_promote_total, chronos_lease_contention_count) and traces documented.

Impact and risk: medium; this changes failover behaviour and is a hotfix after an incident. Mitigations: feature-flag rollout, canary gates, and immediate rollback path. If problems occur, disable chronos.failover_window or reduce snooze window to 0s to fallback to previous behaviour.
